scope: controlled demo API only (http://127.0.0.1:8080) — never a public website

A_normal.expected_behavior: no artificial latency or injected failures

C_checkout_bottleneck.expected_behavior: ~800ms delay on POST /checkout ONLY — GET /products is unaffected
evidence_to_validate: run.thresholdStatus === PASS (products reads stay fast — localization, not blanket latency)
C_checkout_bottleneck.note: Validates MODE SCOPING with a /products plan: checkout_bottleneck must not slow unrelated endpoints. The bottleneck itself is exercised by demo-api/tests and the endpoint selection in k6_scripts with /checkout.

D_error_injection.expected_behavior: ~30% of requests return HTTP 503 (ERROR_INJECTION_FAIL_PERCENT, deterministic hash buckets)

expectation.rationale: closed fixed-VU workload: +~150ms/request latency breaches AND throughput (rps) necessarily falls — the engine must report exactly what the evidence supports, not the single intended dimension

guarded_achievable.condition: if candidate rps degradation stays within 10% (e.g. large VU counts absorbing latency); NOT achievable with the 5 VU/8s plan_defaults workload

expectation.rationale: checkout_bottleneck delays POST /checkout only; a /products-only plan must show no regression (mode scoping, measured)
~30% injected 503s breach the +1pp error-rate policy; latency/rps must NOT be claimed as breaches when the stored evidence does not support them beyond policy

guardrails: never claim exact latency values unless the experiment guarantees them — use ranges/tolerances
the regression engine classifies from stored evidence + policy only; expectations state what the EVIDENCE will support, not desired labels
demo mode is reset to normal after every scenario/case
expected classification for healthy_to_latency_injection is guarded: closed-model rps consequence is part of the honest result
